title: finding(gate): no gate reads the NON-`type` keys of a json fence in `content/docs/**`, so the whole "docs teach a key nothing reads" class is invisible to CI — 4 open cards, one prototype that finds them
body:
Filed unassigned by the `domain:ui` execution seat while implementing objectui#7418 — recording, not claiming. Grading and `domain:*` are the triage seat's.

## The claim

A json fence in `content/docs/**` can author **any key at all** on a node and no gate will object. Only the `type` string is judged. So a documented example that names a real component but authors keys the renderer never reads — or authors an expression on a key that is never evaluated — is green end to end.

## Both gates say so themselves

**`check:doc-types`** scans these pages and judges every `type` literal. Its own header states the exclusion:

> NOT in scope, deliberately: whether the snippet's OTHER keys are read by the renderer the type resolves to. That is objectui#4823's second dimension and needs a per-renderer read-point contract; this gate answers one question only — does the type exist.

**`check:doc-snippets`** does cover these pages — asking its own exported `analyze()` on `origin/main` `3faaa7d0f` returns `content/docs/guide/expressions.md` in `covered`, and it is not in `UNGATED_DOCS` — but it type-checks **ts/tsx blocks only**. The json fences are never compiled against anything.

⇒ Between them: the `type` is checked, the ts/tsx is checked, and the json fence bodies are unchecked.

## The class is recurring, not hypothetical

Four open cards of exactly this shape, each found by a human or an agent re-reading a page, never by CI:

- objectui#7418 — `guide/expressions.md` authors `${…}` on 6 keys with no carriage row. All 6 rendered wrong under green gates. One of them, `badge.text`, is not a `BadgeSchema` key at all and rendered an **empty badge**.
- objectui#7440 — `record-edit-modes.md` teaches an `action:button` with a nested `action` bag that nothing unwraps.
- objectui#7444 — a `color` key on `text` nodes that nothing declares and nothing reads.
- objectui#7838 — `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` teaches an `ObjectRenderer` phantom.

## A prototype that finds them, written for objectui#7418

Roughly 40 lines, no build step beyond the installed spec. It walks every ```json fence, tolerates the `//` comments and the raw newlines inside `${…}` that these pages use, splits fences holding several top-level objects, and for each node with a string `type` flags any string key holding `${…}` that is not in the union of: `content`, the carriage keys for that node's type (read from `expressionBindableTextKeysFor` in the built `@objectstack/spec` artifact — the same lookup `SchemaRenderer` consumes), the `properties` / `props` bags, and the condition keys.

On `guide/expressions.md`: **39 fences, 39 parsed, 0 unparsed.** It reproduced objectui#7418's six sites independently, plus the two `list.items` occurrences that card deliberately left unclaimed — and after the repair reports only those two. Available in that PR's session; happy to hand it over.

Note the prototype answers the **expression** half of the question (is this key evaluated). The wider half — is this key *read back* by the renderer, which is what objectui#7440 and objectui#7444 are — is the per-renderer read-point contract `check:doc-types` names as the missing piece. The expression half is the cheap one and is derivable from an artifact today.

## Why it matters now

objectui#4795's second half — build-time rejection of `${…}` outside the carriage map — reddens sites like these when it lands. A gate on the teaching surface is what keeps the docs from being the last place the rule is not enforced.
